raw_final_content:
The three images show the same robust, strongly convex, oval beetle with reddish- to copper-brown elytra, clear longitudinal elytral grooves/striae, a darker pronotum/head region and stout legs. That combination strongly supports Scarabaeidae (a scarab/chafer).

I would not force a species or even a genus from these photographs. A Melolonthinae-like brown chafer is plausible, but the features that normally separate similar scarabs—antenna and lamellar club, clypeus/head shape, ventral characters, tibial details, exact size and fine punctation—are either hidden or too soft. The correct high-confidence statement is “brown scarab beetle, family Scarabaeidae”; anything more specific should be marked provisional.

A front/side macro of the head and antenna, an underside shot, a sharp fore-tibia image and a ruler-scale dorsal photograph would dramatically improve identification.
